bugs.summary: as() fails to pick up ANY method via S3 inheritance

comments.text:
Converting from r-devel thread: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2026-March/084409.html

Minimal example:

```
setClass("integer64")
setAs("ANY", "integer64", \(from) from)
x <- structure(1e10, class=c("foo", "integer64"))
as(x, "integer64")
# Error in as(x, "integer64") :
#   internal problem in as(): “foo” is(object, "integer64") is TRUE, but the metadata asserts that the 'is' relation is FALSE
```

As Martin pointed out, it's not great that the user can see such "internal problem".

For more context, this was originally seen in the {bit64} package. We had rewritten our `c()` S3 method using `as()` for generic coercion, which we had to refactor to use the S3 `as.*` method directly instead.

 - https://github.com/r-lib/bit64/pull/253
 - https://github.com/r-lib/bit64/pull/302

`setClass("foo")` / `setClass("foo", contains="integer64")` / `setOldClass("foo")` make the issue go away, too, but in context that would be a breaking change to a downstream non-S4 package.

Honestly I'm a bit lost the right solution here, but it _does_ seem like we misused `as()` by employing it in an S3 context.
